claims.text: A nanoscale Mo interlayer deposited by sputtering will improve adhesion at the W-CuCrZr interface.
A nanoscale Mo interlayer will improve the thermal and irradiation stability of the W-CuCrZr interface.
Mo will act as a diffusion barrier between W and CuCrZr.
Mo will mitigate thermal-expansion mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
Thermal-expansion differences at a direct W-CuCrZr interface can cause voids and reduced interfacial integrity.
Chemical incompatibility at a direct W-CuCrZr interface can cause interdiffusion and reduced interfacial integrity.
Fusion-facing materials experience high temperatures and intense particle and neutron irradiation.
Temperatures from 1000 K to 1600 K with concurrent particle irradiation represent relevant test conditions for the proposed W-Mo-CuCrZr interface.
A sputtered Mo layer will form a chemically and mechanically graded W/Mo/CuCrZr interface.
The proposed graded interface will reduce stress concentrations.
The proposed graded interface will inhibit interdiffusion and promote bonding between W and CuCrZr.
Mo bonds well with both W and CuCrZr.
The refractory nature of Mo makes the interlayer robust under high-temperature fusion conditions.
Reduced diffusion and thermal-mismatch stress will mitigate interfacial-defect formation during thermal cycling and irradiation.
Compared with a direct W-CuCrZr bond, the Mo-interlayer system will have greater mechanical stability and less interdiffusion and void formation.
The Mo-interlayer system will retain interfacial integrity better during prolonged high-temperature irradiation.
W-CuCrZr interfaces without an interlayer typically undergo interdiffusion, thermal-stress buildup, defect formation, and degraded fusion-relevant performance.
Mo-interlayer effectiveness may depend on layer thickness, deposition quality, and possible interfacial reactions.
Related studies provide preliminary evidence for qualitative benefits of a Mo interlayer in this application.
